guards.what: HAUNT: Weak first, then five Dazed into the DISCARD pile
guards.rationale: HauntedShip.cs:81-82 applies Weak 3 and then CardPileCmd.AddToCombatAndPreview<Dazed>(targets, PileType.Discard, 5, null). Sim haunted_ship.py:58-60: WeakPower 3, then five CardPileCmd.add_to_discard calls. Pile is Discard on both sides (PROMPT.md class 7's pile-limbo trap does not bite: nothing here is mid-OnPlay), the order Weak-then-Dazed matches, and the count is 5. The one-call-with-count-5 vs five-calls shape is a CardPileCmd-seam question, not a per-monster one; the resulting discard pile is five Dazed either way.

guards.what: StatusIntent(5) loses its count in the sim's Intent
guards.rationale: Presentation surface, waived per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster_state_machine N2/N5 and the KinPriest N6 precedent). Read to the end before waiving: HauntedShip.cs:44 telegraphs `new DebuffIntent(), new StatusIntent(HauntDazed)` - the 5 is the NUMBER SHOWN on the status icon. The sim collapses the pair to Intent(DEBUFF, also=(STATUS_CARD,)) (haunted_ship.py:41) and its Intent dataclass has no status-count field (monsters/base.py:36-51). The move still adds five Dazed; only the telegraphed digit is lost. The AbstractIntent vocabulary mapping is monster_state_machine boundary hole 2 and is audited by no record; flagged here rather than silently skipped.

All 29 PROMPT.md bug classes checked against this unit. Class 6: no branch state. Class 7 (pile limbo): the Dazed go to Discard from a monster move, never mid-OnPlay. Class 8 (append position): AddToCombat appends to the discard pile on both sides; no shuffle is involved, so no StableShuffle tie-order exposure. Class 10: HauntedShip.cs holds no per-combat state field at all. Class 21: neither kills nor is retained.
